Analise o(s) documento(s) de cenário do projeto e gere o SRS completo no formato especificado, seguindo o processo de trabalho: buscas dedicadas na base de conhecimento para cada tipo de artefato, rastreabilidade validada entre os artefatos.

Documento(s) de cenário:
--- Project Scenario 8.pdf ---
BECS (Book E-Commerce System)
So basically what we're trying to do is get books selling 
online instead of however you guys are doing it now, just a 
simple site where people can come in, look through what's 
available, throw a few books in a cart and check out. Nothing 
crazy, I just want it to actually work and not be a headache 
to keep up with. Right now I think it's all kind of manual or 
scattered and there's no real way for someone to just browse 
and buy without someone in the middle handling it, so that's 
the itch we're trying to scratch here. 
 
Anybody coming to the site should be able to just make an 
account, that's it, no big verification process or anything, 
and once they're in they can search for books and see title, 
author, price, add stuff to their cart and go through 
checkout. Keep the search simple, just matching on the title 
and it has to be exact, nothing fancy like partial matches or 
letting people search by author, that's more than we need 
right now. Some of these people might want to sign up to get 
notified about promotions and deals, so let's call those folks 
members, and they're the ones who can use promo codes when 
they check out. I picture this being pretty bare-bones in 
terms of who can buy what, like one copy of each book per 
order is plenty, we don't need people stacking ten copies of 
the same thing in their cart. 
 
On my side of things, I need a way to manage the inventory, 
basically a login that lets me add new books, edit prices, see 
how much stock I've got, that kind of stuff. I also want the 
system to ping me, like an email or something, whenever a book 
is running low so I don't get caught without stock, unless 
I've told it not to bother for that particular book because 
maybe I'm discontinuing it. And I want to be able to set up 
these percentage-off promotions every now and then and have it 
just email all the members automatically when I create one. 
 
One thing I want to be upfront about, we don't need to 
actually process real credit cards or handle real money 
movement right now, just collect the card number as part of 
the checkout flow and spit out a receipt and keep a log of 
what was purchased, who bought it, when. The real payment 
processing piece is something for way later, not part of this. 
Same with security stuff, I know that sounds bad, but honestly 
for what we need right now I'm not worried about encryption or 
people forgetting passwords or whatever, that's not a 
priority, let's not spend time building password recovery or 
anything like that for now. 
 
There's only going to be one person managing the store, me 
basically, so don't worry about building out roles for 
multiple managers or anything fancy like that, and a manager 
should never also be a regular customer account, those are two 
separate hats. It just needs to run somewhere people can get 
to it through a normal browser, nothing exotic on the 
technical side, just something stable that people in here can 
pull up and use without issues.

Sistema: BECS (Book E-Commerce System)

Resumo executivo: BECS is a browser-based book e-commerce system intended to replace manual and fragmented sales activities. It enables customers to create accounts, browse and search books, manage a shopping cart, use member promotions, complete checkout without real payment processing, and receive receipts. A single store manager can maintain the catalog, inventory, low-stock notifications, and percentage-based promotions.

Escopo: Provide online book browsing, ordering, inventory management, and promotional communication through a web browser.
  Em escopo: Customer account registration and authentication
  Em escopo: Book catalog browsing and exact-title search
  Em escopo: Shopping cart management
  Em escopo: Member enrollment and promotional-code usage
  Em escopo: Checkout without real payment authorization
  Em escopo: Receipt generation and purchase logging
  Em escopo: Book catalog, price, and inventory management
  Em escopo: Low-stock email notifications
  Em escopo: Percentage-based promotion management
  Em escopo: Automatic promotional emails to members
  Fora de escopo: Real credit-card authorization and money movement — deferred to a future version
  Fora de escopo: Password recovery — explicitly deprioritized
  Fora de escopo: Encryption functionality — explicitly deprioritized for this version
  Fora de escopo: Complex customer identity verification — not required
  Fora de escopo: Partial-title and author-based search — not required
  Fora de escopo: Multiple store managers or configurable management roles — only one manager is required
  Fora de escopo: Purchasing multiple copies of the same book in one order — prohibited by business policy
  Premissa: PA-01: [INFERRED] An email delivery service will be available for inventory and promotion notifications.
  Premissa: PA-02: Card numbers are collected only to simulate the checkout workflow and are not submitted to a payment processor.
  Premissa: PA-03: [INFERRED] Inventory quantities are represented as non-negative whole numbers.
  Premissa: PA-04: [INFERRED][TBD] The store manager will define the stock quantity considered low for each book.
  Restrição: REST-01 (Technical): The system must be accessible through a standard web browser.
  Restrição: REST-02 (Business): Only one store manager account may exist.
  Restrição: REST-03 (Business): A manager identity cannot also hold a customer or member account.
  Restrição: REST-04 (Functional): Book searches must use exact title matching only.
  Restrição: REST-05 (Payment): The system must not authorize cards or transfer money.
  Restrição: REST-06 (Security): Password recovery and data encryption are outside the current release.

Stakeholders:
  STK-01 - Prospective customer (Primary user): Create a customer account without a complex identity-verification process.
  STK-02 - Registered customer (Primary user): Browse books, search by exact title, manage a cart, complete checkout, and receive a receipt.
  STK-03 - Member (Primary user): Receive promotion notifications and apply valid promotional codes during checkout.
  STK-04 - Store manager (Primary user): Manage books, prices, inventory, low-stock alerts, promotions, and purchase records.
  STK-05 - Email delivery service (External stakeholder): Deliver low-stock alerts and promotional messages generated by BECS.

Regras de negócio:
  RN-001 - Exact-title search: Book searches are performed exclusively by complete and exact title; partial-title and author searches are not accepted.
  RN-002 - Member promotion privilege: Only customers enrolled to receive promotional communications qualify as members and may use promotional codes.
  RN-003 - One copy per order: An order may contain no more than one copy of each book.
  RN-004 - Low-stock notification exception: The manager must be notified when a book reaches low stock unless notifications have been disabled for that book.
  RN-005 - Promotion communication: Creating a percentage-based promotion triggers notification of all enrolled members.
  RN-006 - Simulated payment: Checkout collects a card number but does not authorize payment, transfer funds, or communicate with a real payment processor.
  RN-007 - Purchase record: Every completed order must record the purchased books, purchaser identity, and completion date and time.
  RN-008 - Single manager: The store is administered by exactly one manager.
  RN-009 - Exclusive account types: A manager identity cannot simultaneously be registered as a customer or member identity.
  RN-010 - Stock availability: [INFERRED] A book may be ordered only when at least one copy is available, and its stock quantity cannot become negative.
  RN-011 - Low-stock threshold: [INFERRED][TBD] A book is considered low in stock when its available quantity is equal to or below its configured low-stock threshold.

Requisitos funcionais:
  RF-001 - Customer registration: The system shall register a customer account without requiring an extended identity-verification process. [Must have]
  RF-002 - Customer authentication: The system shall authenticate a registered customer using the credentials provided during registration. [Must have]
  RF-003 - Catalog browsing: The system shall display the books currently available for purchase. [Must have]
  RF-004 - Exact-title search: The system shall return books only when the entered search value exactly matches the complete book title. [Must have]
  RF-005 - Book details: The system shall display the title, author, price, and availability of a selected book. [Must have]
  RF-006 - Member enrollment: The system shall enroll a customer as a member when the customer opts to receive promotional communications. [Should have]
  RF-007 - Add book to cart: The system shall add one available book to the authenticated customer's shopping cart. [Must have]
  RF-008 - Prevent duplicate copies: The system shall reject an attempt to add a second copy of a book already present in the same cart. [Must have]
  RF-009 - View cart: The system shall display the books and calculated subtotal of the authenticated customer's cart. [Must have]
  RF-010 - Remove book from cart: The system shall remove a selected book from the authenticated customer's cart. [Should have]
  RF-011 - Apply promotional code: The system shall accept a valid promotional code during checkout only from an authenticated member. [Should have]
  RF-012 - Calculate promotional discount: The system shall calculate the order discount using the percentage associated with the accepted promotional code. [Should have]
  RF-013 - Collect card number: The system shall collect a card number as part of the checkout form. [Must have]
  RF-014 - Complete simulated checkout: The system shall complete checkout without authorizing the card or transferring funds. [Must have]
  RF-015 - Generate receipt: The system shall generate a receipt after successful checkout. [Must have]
  RF-016 - Log purchase: The system shall record the purchased books, purchaser identity, and checkout date and time for every completed order. [Must have]
  RF-017 - Deduct purchased stock: The system shall reduce the available stock of each purchased book by one after successful checkout. [Must have]
  RF-018 - Manager authentication: The system shall authenticate the single store manager before granting access to management functions. [Must have]
  RF-019 - Add book: The system shall allow the authenticated manager to add a new book to the catalog. [Must have]
  RF-020 - Edit book price: The system shall allow the authenticated manager to edit the price of an existing book. [Must have]
  RF-021 - View stock: The system shall display the available stock quantity of each book to the authenticated manager. [Must have]
  RF-022 - Update stock: The system shall allow the authenticated manager to update the available stock quantity of a book. [Must have]
  RF-023 - Configure low-stock threshold: [INFERRED] The system shall allow the authenticated manager to configure a non-negative low-stock threshold for each book. [Should have]
  RF-024 - Disable low-stock notification: The system shall allow the authenticated manager to disable low-stock notifications for an individual book. [Must have]
  RF-025 - Send low-stock email: The system shall email the manager when an enabled book reaches its low-stock threshold. [Must have]
  RF-026 - Create percentage promotion: The system shall allow the authenticated manager to create a promotional code with a percentage discount. [Must have]
  RF-027 - Notify members of promotion: The system shall email every enrolled member after a percentage-based promotion is created. [Must have]
  RF-028 - Enforce account-type separation: The system shall reject creation of a customer or member account for the manager identity. [Must have]

Requisitos não funcionais:
  RNF-001 (Compatibility) - The system shall complete all critical workflows without blocking defects on the two most recent major versions of Chrome, Firefox, Edge, and Safari. [TBD] | Métrica: 100% of critical registration, browsing, cart, checkout, and management tests pass on 8 browser/version combinations. [TBD]
  RNF-002 (Reliability) - The system shall maintain monthly availability of at least 99.0%, excluding announced maintenance windows. [TBD] | Métrica: Maximum unplanned downtime of 7.3 hours per month. [TBD]
  RNF-003 (Performance Efficiency) - The system shall respond to catalog, search, cart, and inventory requests within 2 seconds at the 95th percentile under 100 concurrent users. [TBD] | Métrica: 95% of measured requests complete within 2 seconds under a load of 100 concurrent users. [TBD]
  RNF-004 (Reliability) - The system shall ensure that 100% of completed orders have a purchase log, receipt, and corresponding stock deduction. | Métrica: Zero inconsistent records across 1,000 simulated checkout transactions. [TBD]
  RNF-005 (Security) - The system shall deny customer and member accounts access to 100% of manager-only functions. | Métrica: Zero successful unauthorized accesses across all management endpoints and user-interface routes.
  RNF-006 (Interaction Capability) - The system shall enable at least 90% of first-time test participants to register, find an exact-title book, add it to the cart, and complete checkout within 5 minutes without assistance. [TBD] | Métrica: Task completion rate of at least 90% within 5 minutes among at least 20 representative participants. [TBD]
  RNF-007 (Maintainability) - The system shall maintain automated test coverage of at least 80% for business-logic statements. [TBD] | Métrica: Business-logic statement coverage greater than or equal to 80%. [TBD]
  RNF-008 (Reliability) - The system shall submit at least 99% of generated low-stock and promotion emails to the configured email service within 60 seconds. [TBD] | Métrica: At least 99% submission success and a maximum submission latency of 60 seconds over 1,000 test messages. [TBD]

Critérios de aceite:
  CA-001 - Dado a visitor provides all required registration data, quando the visitor submits the registration form, então the system creates exactly one customer account without requesting extended identity verification
  CA-002 - Dado a registered customer provides valid credentials, quando the customer submits the login form, então the system establishes an authenticated customer session and displays the catalog
  CA-003 - Dado the catalog contains available and unavailable books, quando an authenticated customer opens the catalog, então the system displays all books with stock greater than zero and excludes books with stock equal to zero
  CA-004 - Dado the catalog contains a book titled 'Example Book', quando the customer searches for the complete value 'Example Book', então the system returns that book; searches for 'Example' or its author return zero matches
  CA-005 - Dado a book exists in the catalog, quando the customer opens its details, então the system displays exactly one title, one author, one price, and one availability status
  CA-006 - Dado an authenticated customer is not a member, quando the customer opts into promotional communications, então the account status changes to 'Member'
  CA-007 - Dado a selected book has stock greater than zero and is not in the cart, quando the customer selects 'Add to cart', então the cart contains exactly one copy of the selected book
  CA-008 - Dado the cart already contains one copy of a book, quando the customer attempts to add the same book again, então the cart quantity remains 1 and the system displays 'Only one copy of each book is allowed per order'
  CA-009 - Dado the cart contains two distinct books priced at 10.00 and 15.00, quando the customer opens the cart, então the system displays both books and a subtotal of 25.00
  CA-010 - Dado the cart contains a selected book, quando the customer requests its removal, então the selected book is absent from the cart and the subtotal is recalculated
  CA-011 - Dado a valid promotional code exists, quando a member submits the code during checkout, então the system accepts the code; the same submission by a non-member displays 'Promotional codes are available to members only'
  CA-012 - Dado a member has a subtotal of 100.00 and an accepted 20% promotional code, quando the checkout total is calculated, então the system displays a discount of 20.00 and a final total of 80.00
  CA-013 - Dado the customer is completing checkout, quando the customer submits the checkout form without a card number, então the system creates zero orders and displays 'Card number is required'
  CA-014 - Dado the cart and checkout data are valid, quando the customer confirms checkout, então the order status becomes 'Completed' without any outbound payment-processor request
  CA-015 - Dado an order has completed successfully, quando checkout is committed, então the system generates exactly one receipt identifying the order and purchased books
  CA-016 - Dado an order completes successfully, quando the purchase log is queried, então exactly one record contains the purchased books, customer identifier, and completion timestamp
  CA-017 - Dado a purchased book has stock quantity 5 before checkout, quando the order completes successfully, então the book's stock quantity becomes exactly 4
  CA-018 - Dado the store manager provides valid manager credentials, quando the manager submits the login form, então the system establishes a manager session and displays the management area
  CA-019 - Dado the authenticated manager provides valid title, author, price, and stock values, quando the manager saves the new book, então exactly one new catalog record is created with the submitted values
  CA-020 - Dado a book has a price of 20.00, quando the manager changes its price to 25.00, então the stored and customer-visible price becomes exactly 25.00
  CA-021 - Dado a book has stock quantity 12, quando the manager opens the inventory view, então the system displays stock quantity 12 for that book
  CA-022 - Dado a book has stock quantity 12, quando the manager updates the quantity to 20, então the stored stock quantity becomes exactly 20
  CA-023 - Dado the manager selects a catalog book, quando the manager sets its low-stock threshold to 3, então the system stores the threshold as exactly 3 and rejects values below 0
  CA-024 - Dado low-stock notifications are enabled for a book, quando the manager disables notifications for that book, então the book's notification status becomes 'Disabled'
  CA-025 - Dado a book has an enabled threshold of 3 and its stock changes from 4 to 3, quando the new stock quantity is stored, então the system submits exactly one low-stock email to the manager within 60 seconds [TBD]
  CA-026 - Dado the manager provides a unique code and a discount of 15%, quando the manager creates the promotion, então the system stores exactly one promotion with the submitted code and percentage 15
  CA-027 - Dado a promotion is created and 50 enrolled members exist, quando promotion creation completes, então the system submits exactly 50 promotional emails, one for each member
  CA-028 - Dado the manager identity already exists, quando registration is attempted using that identity, então zero customer accounts are created and the system displays 'Manager identity cannot be registered as a customer'

Glossário:
  BECS: Book E-Commerce System covered by this specification.
  Customer: A registered person permitted to browse books, manage a cart, and place orders.
  Member: A customer enrolled to receive promotional communications and permitted to use promotional codes.
  Store manager: The single person authorized to manage books, prices, inventory, notifications, and promotions.
  Exact-title search: A search that returns a book only when the entered text matches its complete title.
  Promotional code: A manager-created code that grants members a percentage reduction during checkout.
  Low-stock threshold: The stock quantity at or below which a book is considered low in stock.
  Simulated checkout: An order-completion workflow that collects a card number but performs no card authorization or money transfer.
  Purchase log: The persistent record identifying purchased books, the purchaser, and the order completion date and time.
  Receipt: The document generated after successful checkout to summarize the completed order.

Base: ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 §9.6 · IEEE 830-1998 §3 · Sommerville (2016, cap. 4)
O Documento de Especificação de Requisitos de Software (SRS) é o contrato técnico que descreve o 
que o sistema deve fazer e sob quais condições de qualidade. Ele serve de referência para 
desenvolvedores, testadores, gerentes e clientes durante todo o ciclo de vida do projeto.
1.1 Artefatos Obrigatórios e sua Ordem
Um SRS completo e formal deve conter os seguintes artefatos, nesta ordem:
• ESCOPO: Define o que está DENTRO e FORA do projeto. Evita scope creep.
• STAKEHOLDERS: Lista todos os envolvidos: quem usa, quem financia, quem é afetado.
• PREMISSAS E RESTRIÇÕES: Fatos assumidos como verdadeiros e limites impostos ao projeto.
• REGRAS DE NEGÓCIO (RN): Políticas, fórmulas e condições de negócio que existem independentemente 
do software.
• REQUISITOS FUNCIONAIS (RF): O que o sistema DEVE FAZER — comportamentos, serviços, respostas a 
entradas.
• REQUISITOS NÃO FUNCIONAIS (RNF): Como o sistema deve SER — atributos de qualidade 
quantificáveis.
• HISTÓRIAS DE USUÁRIO (HU): Necessidades na perspectiva do usuário: Como [perfil], quero [ação], para
[benefício].
• CASOS DE USO (UC): Interações detalhadas ator-sistema com fluxo principal, alternativo e exceções.
• CRITÉRIOS DE ACEITE (CA): Condições testáveis em formato BDD (Dado/Quando/Então) que definem 
quando o requisito está concluído.
• GLOSSÁRIO: Termos do domínio com definição precisa para eliminar ambiguidades.
1.2 Como os Artefatos se Interconectam
Os artefatos formam uma cadeia de rastreabilidade. Cada RF deve ter origem em um STK 
(stakeholder) ou RN. Cada HU deve ter pelo menos um RF associado. Cada RF e HU devem ter pelo menos um CA. Esta rastreabilidade garante que nada seja implementado sem justificativa de 
negócio e que tudo que foi prometido seja testável.
Cadeia de rastreabilidade mínima:
STK → (RN →) RF → HU → CA

Rastrear os Requisitos PE (5.1)
Propósito
O objetivo de Rastrear os Requisitos é garantir que os requisitos e designs em 
diferentes níveis estejam alinhados entre si e gerenciar os efeitos da 
mudança em um nível nos requisitos relacionados.
Descrição
Rastrear os Requisitos: analisa e mantém os relacionamentos entre 
requisitos, designs, componentes de solução e outros produtos de trabalho 
para análise de impacto, cobertura e alocação.
Entradas
• Requisitos: podem ser rastreados para outros requisitos (incluindo 
metas, objetivos, requisitos de negócio, requisitos de stakeholder, 
requisitos de solução e requisitos de transição), componentes de 
solução, recursos visuais, regras de negócio e outros produtos de 
trabalho.
• Designs: podem ser rastreados para outros requisitos, componentes de 
solução e outros produtos de trabalho.
Saídas 
• Requisitos (rastreados): têm relações claramente definidas com outros 
requisitos, componentes de solução ou versões, fases ou iterações, 
dentro de um escopo de solução, de modo que a cobertura e os efeitos da 
mudança sejam claramente identificáveis.
• Designs (rastreados): relacionamentos claramente definidos com outros 
requisitos, componentes da solução ou versões, fases ou iterações,

SRS described just the differences that the new version should exhibit compared to the previous 
version. Nowhere was there a description of the original system. Consequently, everyone had a 
different understanding of the current system’s capabilities. If you’re in this situation, document 
the requirements for your project more thoroughly so that all the stakeholders—both present 
and future—understand what the system does.
Expected challenges
The presence of an existing system leads to common challenges that both enhancement and 
replacement projects will face, including the following:
■ The changes made could degrade the performance to which users are accustomed.
■ Little or no requirements documentation might be available for the existing system.
■ Users who are familiar with how the system works today might not like the changes they are 
about to encounter.
■ You might unknowingly break or omit functionality that is vital to some stakeholder group.
■ Stakeholders might take this opportunity to request new functionality that seems like a good 
idea but isn’t really needed to meet the business objectives.
Even if there is existing documentation, it might not prove useful. For enhancement projects, 
the documentation might not be up to date. If the documentation doesn’t match the existing 
application’s reality, it is of limited use. For replacement systems, you also need to be wary of carrying 
forward all of the requirements, because some of the old functionality probably should not be 
migrated.
One of the major issues in replacement projects is validating that the reasons for the replacement 
are sound. There need to be justifiable business objectives for the change. When existing systems 
are being completely replaced, organizational processes might also have to change, which makes it 
harder for people to accept a new system. The change in business processes, change in the software 
system, and learning curve of a new system can disrupt current operations.

Most older systems do not have documented—let alone accurate—requirements. In the absence of 
reliable documentation, teams might reverse-engineer an understanding of what the system does 
from the user interfaces, code, and database. We think of this as “software archaeology.” To maximize 
the benefit from reverse engineering, the archaeology expedition should record what it learns in 
the form of requirements and design descriptions. Accumulating accurate information about certain 
portions of the current system positions the team to enhance a system with low risk, to replace a 
system without missing critical functionality, and to perform future enhancements efficiently. It halts 
the knowledge drain, so future maintainers better understand the changes that were just made.
If updating the requirements is overly burdensome, it will fall by the wayside as busy people rush 
on to the next change request. Obsolete requirements aren’t helpful for future enhancements. There’s 
a widespread fear in the software industry that writing documentation will consume too much time; 
the knee-jerk reaction is to neglect all opportunities to update requirements documentation. But 
what’s the cost if you don’t update the requirements and a future maintainer (perhaps you!) has to 
regenerate that information? The answer to this question will let you make a thoughtful business 
decision concerning whether to revise the requirements documentation when you change or 
re-create the software.
When the team performs additional enhancements and maintenance over time, it can extend 
these fractional knowledge representations, steadily improving the system documentation. The 
incremental cost of recording this newly found knowledge is small compared with the cost of 
someone having to rediscover it later on. Implementing enhancements almost always necessitates 
further requirements development, so add those new requirements to an existing requirements 
repository, if there is one. If you’re replacing an old system, you have an opportunity to document 
the requirements for the new one and to keep the requirements up to date with what you learn 
throughout the project. Try to leave the requirements in better shape than you found them.
Which requirements should you specify?
It’s not always worth taking the time to generate a complete set of requirements for an entire 
production system. Many options lie between the two extremes of continuing forever with no 
requirements documentation and reconstructing a perfect requirements set. Knowing why you’d like 
to have written requirements available lets you judge whether the cost of rebuilding all—or even 
part—of the specification is a sound investment.

If developers build exactly what 
customers initially request, they’ll probably have to build it again because customers often don’t 
know what they really need. In addition, the BAs might not be talking to the right people or asking 
the right questions.
The features that users present as their “wants” don’t necessarily equate to the functionality they 
need to perform their tasks with the new product. To gain a more accurate view of user needs, the 
business analyst must collect a wide range of user input, analyze and clarify it, and specify just what 
needs to be built to let users do their jobs. The BA has the lead responsibility for recording the new 
system’s necessary capabilities and properties and for communicating that information to other 
stakeholders. This is an iterative process that takes time. If you don’t invest the time to achieve this 
shared understanding—this common vision of the intended product—the certain outcomes are 
rework, missed deadlines, cost overruns, and customer dissatisfaction.
User classes
People often talk about “the user” for a software system as though all users belong to a monolithic 
group with similar characteristics and needs. In reality, most products of any size appeal to a diversity 
of users with different expectations and goals. Rather than thinking of “the user” in singular, spend 
some time identifying the multiple user classes and their roles and privileges for your product.
Classifying users
Chapter 2 described many of the types of stakeholders that a project might have. As shown in 
Figure 6-1, a user class is a subset of the product’s users, which is a subset of the product’s customers, 
which is a subset of its stakeholders. An individual can belong to multiple user classes. For example, 
an application’s administrator might also interact with it as an ordinary user at times. A product’s 
users might differ—among other ways—in the following respects, and you can group users into a 
number of distinct user classes based on these sorts of differences:
■ Their access privilege or security levels (such as ordinary user, guest user, administrator)
■ The tasks they perform during their business operations
■ The features they use
■ The frequency with which they use the product
■ Their application domain experience and computer systems expertise
■ The platforms they will be using (desktop PCs, laptop PCs, tablets, smartphones, specialized 
devices)CHAPTER 6 Finding the voice of the user 103
■ Their native language
■ Whether they will interact with the system directly or indirectly
FIGURE 6-1 A hierarchy of stakeholders, customers, users, and user classes.
It’s tempting to group users into classes based on their geographical location or the kind of 
company they work in. One company that creates software used in the banking industry initially 
considered distinguishing users based on whether they worked in a large commercial bank, a small 
commercial bank, a savings and loan institution, or a credit union. These distinctions really represent 
different market segments, though, not different user classes.
A better way to identify user classes is to think about the tasks that various users will perform with 
the system. All of those types of financial institutions will have tellers, employees who process loan 
applications, business bankers, and so forth. The individuals who perform such activities—whether 
they are job titles or simply roles—will have similar functional needs for the system across all of the 
financial institutions. Tellers all have to do more or less the same things, business bankers do more or 
less the same things, and so on. More logical user class names for a banking system therefore might 
include teller, loan officer, business banker, and branch manager. You might discover additional user 
classes by thinking of possible use cases, user stories, and process flows and who might perform them.

- Any visitor can create an account with no verification process.

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: The visitor does not have a customer account.
fluxo_principal: 1. The actor opens the registration page.
2. The actor enters the required account data.
3. The system validates the submitted data.
4. The system creates the customer account.
fluxos_alternativos: 2a. The actor opts into promotional communications → the system marks the account as a member; continues at step 3.
fluxos_excecao: 3a. The identity belongs to the manager → the system displays 'Manager identity cannot be registered as a customer' and creates no account (RN-009, RF-028).

casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: The exactly matching book is displayed.
fluxo_principal: 1. The actor opens the catalog search.
2. The actor enters a complete book title.
3. The system performs an exact-title comparison.
4. The system displays the matching book.
fluxos_alternativos: 4a. No exact match exists → the system displays 'No book found'; the use case ends.
fluxos_excecao: 2a. The search value is empty → the system displays 'Enter a complete book title' and returns to step 2 (RN-001, RF-004).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: The customer is authenticated and the selected book has available stock.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: One copy of the book is present in the cart.
fluxo_principal: 1. The actor selects an available book.
2. The actor requests to add the book to the cart.
3. The system verifies that the book is not already in the cart.
4. The system adds one copy to the cart.
fluxos_excecao: 3a. The book is already in the cart → the system displays 'Only one copy of each book is allowed per order' and leaves the cart unchanged (RN-003, RF-008).
3b. The book has no available stock → the system displays 'Book unavailable' and leaves the cart unchanged (RN-010, RF-007).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: The member is authenticated and has at least one book in the cart.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: The discount is applied to the order total.
fluxo_principal: 1. The actor starts checkout.
2. The actor enters a promotional code.
3. The system validates the actor's member status and the code.
4. The system calculates and displays the discounted total.
fluxos_excecao: 3a. The actor is not a member → the system displays 'Promotional codes are available to members only' (RN-002, RF-011).
3b. The code is invalid → the system displays 'Invalid promotional code' and leaves the total unchanged (RF-011).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: The customer is authenticated and the cart contains at least one available book.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: The order, receipt, purchase log, and stock deductions are recorded.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_falha: No order or stock change is committed.
fluxo_principal: 1. The actor reviews the cart.
2. The actor enters a card number.
3. The actor confirms checkout.
4. The system records the order without contacting a payment processor.
5. The system deducts one stock unit for each purchased book.
6. The system records the purchase log.
7. The system generates and displays the receipt.
fluxos_alternativos: 2a. The actor is a member with a valid promotional code → the system applies the percentage discount; returns to step 3.
fluxos_excecao: 2b. No card number is provided → the system displays 'Card number is required' and returns to step 2 (RN-006, RF-013).
4a. A book is no longer available → the system displays 'One or more books are unavailable' and commits no order or stock change (RN-010, RF-014).

casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: The new book is stored in the catalog.
fluxo_principal: 1. The actor opens book management.
2. The actor enters the book title, author, price, and initial stock.
3. The system validates the values.
4. The system adds the book to the catalog.
fluxos_excecao: 3a. The price or stock is negative → the system displays 'Price and stock must be non-negative' and returns to step 2 (RN-010, RF-019).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: The manager is authenticated and the book exists.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: The book contains the new stock quantity.
fluxo_principal: 1. The actor selects a book.
2. The system displays its current stock.
3. The actor enters a new stock quantity.
4. The system validates and stores the quantity.
fluxos_excecao: 4a. The quantity is negative or not a whole number → the system displays 'Stock must be a non-negative whole number' and returns to step 3 (RN-010, RF-022).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: The manager is authenticated and the book exists.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: The threshold and notification preference are stored.
fluxo_principal: 1. The actor selects a book.
2. The actor enters a low-stock threshold.
3. The actor enables or disables low-stock notification.
4. The system stores the configuration.
fluxos_alternativos: 3a. Notification is disabled → the system stores the book as exempt from low-stock emails.
fluxos_excecao: 2a. The threshold is negative → the system displays 'Threshold must be non-negative' and returns to step 2 (RN-011, RF-023).

casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: The promotion is created and notification emails are submitted for all members.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_falha: No promotion or member notification is created.
fluxo_principal: 1. The actor opens promotion management.
2. The actor enters a promotional code and percentage discount.
3. The system validates the promotion.
4. The system creates the promotion.
5. The system submits a promotional email for every enrolled member.
fluxos_excecao: 3a. The percentage is outside the range of 0 exclusive to 100 inclusive → the system displays 'Discount must be greater than 0% and no more than 100%' and returns to step 2 (RN-005, RF-026).

em_escopo: Account creation for any visitor, with no verification process
Book search by exact title match (logged-in users)
Viewing book title, author, and price
Shopping cart with a limit of one copy per book per order
Checkout flow that collects a card number, generates a receipt, and logs the purchase
Member signup to receive promotion notifications and use promo codes at checkout
Manager login to manage inventory (add books, edit prices, view stock)
Automatic low-stock email alert to the manager, with per-book opt-out
Manager-created percentage-off promotions with automatic email to all members
fora_de_escopo: Real credit card / payment processing — deferred to a later phase
Encryption — not a priority for this version
Password recovery — not a priority for this version
Multiple manager accounts or manager roles — only one manager
Partial/fuzzy search or search by author — title search is exact-match only
Multiple copies of the same book per order — limited to one
premissas: PA-01: Only one person will operate the manager account for the store.
restricoes: REST-01 (Tecnica): The system must be usable through a normal web browser, with no exotic client-side requirements.

stakeholders.descricao: Store Manager — the single account responsible for managing inventory (add books, edit prices, view stock) and creating promotions; must never also be a regular customer account.
Visitor — anyone arriving at the site who can create an account with no verification process.
Registered User / Customer — logged-in user who can search for books, add them to a cart, and check out.
Member — a registered user who opted in to promotion notifications; the only type of user who can apply promo codes at checkout.

regras_de_negocio.descricao: A cart may contain at most one copy of each distinct book per order.
A manager account must never also function as a regular customer account.
Only members (not all registered users) can apply promo codes at checkout.
The low-stock email alert to the manager is suppressed for a given book if the manager has disabled notifications for that specific book.
Creating a new percentage-off promotion automatically triggers an email to all members.

requisitos_funcionais.descricao: The system must allow any visitor to create an account with no verification process.
The system must allow logged-in users to search for books by title using an exact match only (no partial match, no search by author).
The system must display each book's title, author, and price.
The system must allow users to add a book to their shopping cart.
The system must prevent a user from adding more than one copy of the same book to their cart in a single order.
The system must allow users to complete checkout for the items in their cart.
The system must allow a registered user to sign up as a member to receive promotion notifications.
The system must allow members to apply a promo code during checkout.
The system must provide a login for the manager, separate from customer accounts.
The system must allow the manager to add new books to the inventory.
The system must allow the manager to edit the price of existing books.
The system must allow the manager to view current stock levels.
The system must send an email notification to the manager when a book's stock is low, unless notifications are disabled for that book.
The system must allow the manager to create percentage-off promotions.
The system must automatically email all members when a new promotion is created.
The system must collect a card number during checkout without processing an actual payment.
The system must generate a receipt after checkout.
The system must log each purchase, including the item, the buyer, and the timestamp.

requisitos_nao_funcionais.descricao: The system must be usable through a standard web browser, with no exotic or non-standard client-side requirements.

historias_de_usuario.descricao: As a visitor, I want to create an account with no verification process, so that I can start using the site quickly.
As a registered user, I want to search for a book by its exact title, so that I can find the book I'm looking for.
As a registered user, I want to view a book's title, author, and price, so that I can decide whether to buy it.
As a registered user, I want to add a book to my cart, so that I can purchase it later.
As a registered user, I want to check out my cart, so that I can complete my purchase.
As a member, I want to apply a promo code at checkout, so that I can get a discount.
As the manager, I want to add new books and edit their prices, so that I can keep the catalog up to date.
As the manager, I want to be notified when a book's stock is low, so that I can restock in time.
As the manager, I want to create percentage-off promotions, so that I can attract more sales.
As a member, I want to receive an email when a new promotion is created, so that I know about current deals.

casos_de_uso.descricao: Search and Purchase Book — a logged-in user searches for a book by exact title, adds it to the cart, and completes checkout.
Manage Inventory — the manager logs in and adds new books, edits prices, or views current stock levels.
Create Promotion — the manager creates a percentage-off promotion, and the system automatically emails all members.

criterios_de_aceite.descricao: Given a logged-in user, when they search for a book title that exactly matches an existing book, then the system returns that book with its title, author, and price.
Given a user already has one copy of a book in their cart, when they try to add another copy of the same book, then the system prevents the second copy from being added.
Given a member is at checkout with a valid promo code, when they apply the code, then the system applies the corresponding discount.
Given a book's stock drops below the defined threshold and notifications are enabled for that book, when the stock update occurs, then the system sends an email to the manager.
Given the manager creates a new percentage-off promotion, when the promotion is saved, then the system automatically sends an email to all members.
